subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar adopt opt-in, user-configured external command hooks as a supported app and CLI contract after the argv editor defect is fixed?
rationale: The patch is not merely an internal repair: it adds durable configuration, UI and CLI surface, and intentional local command execution, so code review cannot decide whether that capability belongs in the product.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow hook contract
options.body: Accept the six opt-in events and existing direct-exec security model after the argument editor preserves argv exactly.

options.title: Narrow the exposed surface
options.body: Keep hooks config- or CLI-managed and omit the graphical rule editor until a safer structured editing experience is designed.

options.title: Decline local command execution
options.body: Keep CodexBar focused on observation and notifications and leave external automation to downstream tools consuming existing output.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow hook contract
recommendation.body: Accept the six opt-in events and existing direct-exec security model after the argument editor preserves argv exactly.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-level product and security-boundary acceptance is required for this new persistent execution surface.
